pr_title: Allow node addresses to be used as loadBalancer addresses for proxy-mode=ipvs
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

To use node-addresses as loadBalancerIP works with proxy-mode=iptables and did work before K8s v1.23 for proxy-mode=ipvs.

A problem with kernel versions and netlink fixed in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101429 caused the problem reported in #114815. The addresses assigned for NodePort became `AllAddresses - addresses(kube-ipvs0)`, but the the node-address is a loadBalancerIP it is assigned (also) to kube-ipvs0 and is thus excluded.

The security fix in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108460 prevents access to ports on the node (like ssh) to be accesible via loadBalancerIPs and clusterIPs, but if a loadBalancerIPs is also a node-ip, then **access to the node will be blocked**.

Both these problems must be taken care of in this PR.


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #114815, #117613

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

**NOTE** I am splitting this PR into one for the cleanup https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115073 and will re-build this PR on top of that.



#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixes a 1.26 regression in kube-proxy ipvs mode
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

Hello, 
We still have the issue on our bare-metal server in 1.27.5 and 1.28.3.

If we force 1.25 everything is working fine.

Did we miss something ?
BR

For proxy-mode=ipvs ServiceIPs (clusterIP, externalIP and loadBalancerIPs) *must* be assigned to a (any) local interface, normally `kube-ipvs0`. This PR makes sure that if a ServiceIP is already assigned to an interface, which should be the case if a node-ip is used as a ServiceIP, then it will _not_ be assigned to `kube-ipvs0`.

In a clean installation of K8s v1.28.x, can you see a ServiceIP (which is also a nodeIP) assigned to _both_ `kube-ipvs0` _and_ another interface (e.g. eth0)?

Also, is your cluster a single-node cluster?
Please see also https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray/issues/10572#issuecomment-1785451612

issue_context.title: kube-proxy v1.26 blocks host services
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We run some Kubernetes “single-node clusters” that combine the control-plane and the workload onto a single host besides some services installed directly on the operating system (SSH, BIND9). With the upgrade to v1.26, all local services become unreachable as soon as kube-proxy configures the network stack. This happens because kube-proxy adds the node’s IP address to the ipset `KUBE-IPVS-IPS`.

We configure the node IP address explicitly for `kubelet`:

```shell
KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--container-runtime-endpoint=unix:///run/cri-dockerd.sock --node-ip=10.169.8.6
```

Also, `kube-proxy` is configured to exclude the node IP address explicitly:

```yaml

    ipvs:
      excludeCIDRs:
      - 10.169.8.6/32
```

@liaralabs has collected more information in https://github.com/k3s-io/k3s/issues/7183#issuecomment-1491205024.

Overriding the `iptables` rules from `kube-proxy` with a higher-priority rules makes the services reachable again. Also, removing the node’s IP address from the `ipset` helps (until kube-proxy syncs the set again).

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy should keep away from node-local services.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Setup a minimal one-node cluster with `kubeadm` and configure it for `ipvs`.
- Add a `Service` of type `LoadBalancer` with `externalIPs` configured.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

comments: Downgrading to v1.25 helped to become the systems operational again.

Most likely related https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815, please see especially https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815#issuecomment-1383804926. This PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115019 could fix the problem in one-node systems.

> kube-proxy should keep away from node-local services

What is "node-local services"? A service that has the (real) node address as externalIP or loadBalancerIP?

> What is "node-local services"? A service that has the (real) node address as externalIP or loadBalancerIP?

Let me rephrase: `kube-proxy` shall not interfere with applications running on the host. I.e., the node IP address should never be blocked even if used as `externalIP` or `loadBalancerIP`. Also, the IP should be completely ignored for the packetfilter when listed in `excludeCIDRs`.
PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115019 is updated and seem to work on K8s master.

```
    ipvs:
      excludeCIDRs:
      - 10.169.8.6/32
```
This is [documented](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kube-proxy-config.v1alpha1/) as:
```
excludeCIDRs is a list of CIDR's which the ipvs proxier should not touch when cleaning up ipvs services.
```
From what I can see it has no relevance in this problem.

This issue is fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115019, which is merged and will be released in v1.28.

I leave this issue open since I suspect there will be a request for back port. I don't know the procedure for that.

review_comments: I'm not familiar with the ipvs proxy, is it creating a new IP address on this dummy interface for the virtualips that doesn't exist on the node?

It's for all VIP addresses. This is the worst with ipvs, it's using some pre-historic hook in the kernel that _requires_ that the address actually exist on an (any) interface on the host. It would be soooo much better if there was a "-j IPVS" target for instance. But, no :angry: Sorry for the rant...

Anyway, all VIPs including ClusterIP, externalIPs and loadBlancerIPs must be assigned to an interface. Normally that is `kube-ipvs0` which is a dummy interface and should be "DOWN". The problem is that K3s, and others perhaps, use the node-ip as externalIP or loadBlancerIPs. Then the address MUST NOT be assigned to `kube-ipvs0`.

This is possible [only for single-node systems](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815#issuecomment-1382090138), so its an odd case but should be supported according to [Hyumes law](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114815#issuecomment-1372411718).

there is another dimension, GCP loadbalancers insert a route to the VIP like this
```
local 34.79.233.109 dev eth0 table local proto 66 scope host
```

```
ip route get 34.79.233.109
local 34.79.233.109 dev lo src 34.79.233.109 uid 20162
    cache <local>
```

this VIP doesn't seem to be associated to any interface
```
 $ ip add | grep 34
 $
```
